hero.title:
One desktop.
Two screens.
hero.lead: Your Android tablet or phone becomes a real second monitor for your Mac. Free and open source, and the OpenDisplay Mac app stays exactly as it is.
specs: macOS via the original OpenDisplay app
hero.stripAlt: A Mac desktop running on past its edge onto an Android tablet beside it, with a window across the seam

howItWorks.title: The Mac stays untouched. The Android device does the listening.
howItWorks.sub: The Android device listens and the Mac connects — that's what lets it work over WiFi with zero manual setup, via mDNS discovery, without a single change to the original OpenDisplay Mac app.

install.title: Two apps that work together.
install.sub: Install both to get going — the Mac side is the original OpenDisplay project, unmodified.

mac.title: The sender
mac.desc: Captures a virtual display and streams it. It's the original OpenDisplay program, unmodified.
mac.note: Prefer to build it yourself? <compile>Build from source ↗</compile>

android.title: The receiver
android.desc: Displays the stream and sends touch/scroll back.

features.title: What already works today.
features.sub: Validated against the real Mac app, not a spec sheet.

items.title: Hardware H.264 video
items.desc: MediaCodec decoding straight to a Surface, no CPU conversion.

items.title: Automatic discovery
items.desc: mDNS (_opensidecar._tcp) — the Mac finds the Android device on its own on the same network.

items.title: Touch and scroll
items.desc: One finger becomes a click/drag, two fingers become scroll — in Extend mode. The Mac's Mirror mode is view-only: it silently ignores input from any client.

items.title: Pinch to zoom
items.desc: Two fingers spread on the video zoom in locally, on either Mirror or Extend mode — no protocol change needed, and touch still lands on the right spot on the Mac. Once zoomed, drag with three fingers to move around the magnified area.

items.title: Remote cursor
items.desc: A dot or decoded sprite, mirroring the Mac's cursor position live.

items.title: Foreground service
items.desc: Survives the app going to background and resumes correctly after unlocking the screen.

items.title: Error recovery
items.desc: Decoder errors trigger an automatic keyframe request, without dropping the connection.

items.title: Manual fallback
items.desc: Editable mDNS name and IP:port connection for when automatic discovery fails.

items.title: USB accessory (AOA)
items.desc: Plug the cable, tap the system's prompt, done — no adb, no developer options.

items.title: Picture-in-Picture
items.desc: Leave the app while connected and the video keeps playing in a floating window.

items.title: No account, no telemetry
items.desc: Same philosophy as the original project: no central server, nothing phoned home.

compare.title: Against the best-known alternatives.
compare.sub: For using an Android tablet as an external monitor.

items.q: Is this the same app as OpenDisplay for iOS?
items.a: No. It's an independent client, written from scratch in Kotlin, that implements the same network protocol to interoperate with the original Mac app. The official project only ships an iOS/iPadOS client.
Yes. OpenDisplay Android is on <play>Google Play ↗</play>.

It works over WiFi with automatic mDNS discovery. You can also connect over USB as a native accessory (AOA) — plug the cable and tap the system's prompt, no adb required. See the repository for a fallback covering Mac apps without AOA support yet.

items.q: Does touch work in Mirror mode?
items.a: No — Mirror mode on the Mac is view-only. The Mac app only accepts touch/scroll in Extend mode (it never builds its input injector for a mirror session), so taps and scrolls sent from here are silently ignored. Use Extend mode for anything interactive.

items.q: Does it work on any Android tablet or phone?
items.a: Requires Android 8.0 (API 26) or higher. Tested on real hardware (Samsung Galaxy Tab S9 FE+ and Galaxy Note10+/Tab S7+, Android 12 through 16), but not yet across a wide range of devices — touch/scroll/cursor are implemented but with limited field validation so far. Note: v0.0.7 and earlier crash on launch on Android 12–13 (API 30-33); use v0.0.8 or newer (fixed in <pr5>#5</pr5>).

items.q: Does it change anything on the Mac app?
items.a: No modification whatsoever — any protocol mismatch is this project's responsibility, not upstream's.
GPL-3.0, same as the original project. Open source, free to use including commercially; distributed modified versions must remain open source under the same license.

contribute.title: Issues and pull requests welcome.
contribute.desc: Bug reports and PRs go on the <repo>GitHub repository</repo>, which also has the architecture, protocol and build details. Careful bug reports are what actually make a one-person side project better — thanks to everyone below.

support.title: If OpenDisplay Android saved you a monitor, consider buying me a coffee.
support.p1: This is a one-person side project, built and maintained by me, <profile>Jose Pacelli</profile>, evenings and weekends — not a company.
support.p2: Supporting me on Ko-fi keeps this project maintained and free for everyone, including people who can't afford to chip in. My goal is to make this the best free way to turn a spare Android tablet into a real second monitor.
support.p3: If it saved you from buying a monitor, a small tip helps keep it going. Thank you.

footer.disclaimer: Not affiliated with the maintainer of the original OpenDisplay project. Speaks the same protocol, maintained separately.
